itens.t: SpaceX Successfully Catches Starship Upper Stage for First Time During Flight 15
itens.r: SpaceX has completed the 15th test flight of its massive Starship rocket from Starbase, Texas, achieving a historic milestone. For the first time ever, the company successfully caught the vehicle's upper stage using the 'Mechazilla' launch tower arms. The ambitious flight test also provided breathtaking footage of the spacecraft's reentry, flip, and relight maneuvers. While the booster experienced issues leading to an explosion due to low fuel, the successful upper-stage catch marks a monumental leap forward in rocket reusability.
itens.d:
SpaceX has completed the 15th test flight of its Starship rocket from the Starbase facility in South Texas. The mission aimed to recover both stages of the vehicle back to the launch site.

While the Super Heavy booster was diverted to an off-shore splashdown and explosion, the upper stage successfully survived orbit and atmospheric re-entry. The launch tower executed a picture-perfect catch of the Ship, marking a major milestone toward full reusability.
itens.e:
SpaceX has completed the 15th test flight of its Starship rocket from the Starbase facility in South Texas, with the mission aiming to recover both stages back to the launch site. During the test, the Super Heavy booster was diverted to an off-shore splashdown and explosion, while the upper stage successfully survived orbit and atmospheric re-entry. This culminated in the launch tower executing a picture-perfect catch of the Ship.

This achievement marks a major milestone toward full reusability for the program. The successful catch directly affects the aerospace industry and the commercial viability of heavy-lift rocketry by demonstrating unprecedented recovery techniques for orbital-class upper stages.

This suggests future tests will focus on refining the booster recovery phase alongside the successfully demonstrated upper-stage catch. One thing to watch next is whether subsequent flights can achieve simultaneous recoveries of both the Super Heavy booster and the Ship to the launch site.

itens.t: Voyager 1 Nears Historic Milestone of One Light-Day From Earth
